This is a crop of a scanned # San Francisco zoning map, # x # pixels (origin top-left).
A district code (read as "{code}") is printed at the centre, circled in red.

Step #. Read the circled code exactly as printed (for example RH-#, RM-#, NC-#, P) into code_read.

Step #. Find the area the code names. Areas are bounded by heavy, thick lines (district boundaries).
Usually the code is printed inside its own area, with no leader.

But a small or narrow area cannot hold its code, so the code is printed just outside it and tied to
it by a leader. On these maps leaders look like:
- a short thin line or curve from the letters into a small area outlined by heavy lines nearby
  (a single lot or a small box), often ending in a small arrowhead;
- a bracket "{", "(" or ")" beside the letters, facing a narrow strip;
- an arrow from the letters to a spot across a street.
Not leaders: the hyphen inside the code (RH-#), a heavy boundary line (never follow one), or letters
that simply overlap a line.

Look closely at the thin strokes touching or right next to the letters before deciding.

If there is a leader, give the pixel where it ends, inside the area it names (at the arrowhead, just
past the end of the line, or inside the strip or box the bracket faces). Otherwise answer has_leader
false and give the code's own centre.

(effort: high)

This is a crop of a #-bit scan of San Francisco's # zoning map, enlarged #x.
Somewhere near the centre (marked by four small red ticks at the edges of the image), a zoning
district code is printed in bold capitals, possibly rotated or italic. Lot numbers (plain digits),
street names and district boundary lines are also printed; they are not codes.

Read the district code printed nearest the centre, character by character. Look closely at digits:
#, #, # and # differ; RH and RM differ (H has two straight uprights; M has a V in the middle).
Codes on this map are usually one of: P, RH-#, RH-#(D), RH-#(S), RH-#, RH-#, RM-#, RM-#, RM-#, RM-#, RC-#, RC-#, RC-#, RC-#, NC-#, NC-#, NC-#, NC-S, NCD, M-#, M-#, C-#, C-#, C-M, C-#-G, C-#-O, C-#-R, C-#-S, SLI, SLR, SSO, RED, CCB, CVR, RSD, SPD, MB-O — or a named district such as
"UNION NCD". If no district code is printed within about a quarter of the image from the centre,
answer "NONE". Give "code" exactly as printed (normalised to that list's spelling when it matches).
(effort: high)

This is a crop of a scanned # San Francisco zoning map, # x # pixels (origin top-left).
The district code "{code}" is printed at the centre, circled in red.

On these maps a code is usually printed inside the area it names. But when that area is too small or
too narrow (a commercial strip along a street, a single small lot), the code is printed beside it and
tied to it by a leader: a thin line, a curved line, an arrow, or a bracket such as "{" or ")" drawn
next to the letters.

Heavy, thick lines are district boundaries, never leaders: do not follow them. A leader is a thin
line or an arrow starting at the letters. A bracket points into the area immediately beside it,
usually a narrow strip just past the bracket.

Does this code have such a leader? If yes, give the pixel where the leader ends: the point inside the
area the code names (at the arrowhead, or just past the end of the line or the bracket's tip). If the
code simply sits inside its area, answer has_leader false and give the code's own centre.

This image is a crop of a scanned historic San Francisco zoning district map. It is # pixels wide and # pixels high. Return x and y as integer pixel coordinates within this image (x from # to #, y from # to #, origin at the top-left).

The map divides the city into zoning districts: areas outlined by heavy lines, each with a district code printed inside it, often in large letters. Find every printed zoning district code:
- kind "use": use-district codes such as R-#, R-#-D, R-#, R-#, R-#, R-#, C-#, C-#, C-#-O, C-M, M-#, M-#, P, RH-#, RH-#(D), RH-#, RH-#, RM-#, RM-#, RC-#, NC-#, NC-#, NC-#, NC-S, CVR, SSO, RED, or neighborhood district names abbreviated as codes (for example "UPPER MARKET NCD").
- kind "height": height-and-bulk district codes such as #-X, #-A, #-B, #-E, #-F, or OS (open space).

For each code give the text exactly as printed, its kind, the pixel center (x, y) of the printed code, and a confidence from # to #.

Ignore block numbers (plain #-# digit numbers), street names, lot numbers and dimensions, legend text, titles and notes. If a code is cut off by the image edge, skip it. Return an empty list rather than guessing.
